chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, who said:

I heard Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: Verily there is a known boundary for the location of the grave of Ḥusain ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him); whoever knows it and seeks refuge in it will be protected. I said, 'Describe its boundary for me, may I be your ransom.' He replied, 'Wipe from the location of his grave today, and wipe twenty-five ells from the side of his feet, and twenty-five ells from what faces his face, and twenty-five ells from behind him, and twenty-five ells from the side of his head. And the location of his grave, since the day he was buried, is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and from it is a ladder by which the deeds of his visitors ascend to the heavens. So there is no angel nor prophet in the heavens except that they ask Allah for permission to go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him). So a crowd descends and a crowd ascends.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance and boundary of Imam al-Husayn's grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) delineates the specific spatial dimensions of the Ḥā’ir, establishing it as a sanctified zone where seeking refuge guarantees divine protection. This narration underscores the cosmological significance of Karbala, portraying the grave not merely as a burial site but as a 'garden of Paradise' and a spiritual ascension point (Mi‘raj) for the deeds of visitors. The text highlights the universal reverence for this site, noting that even prophets and angels seek permission to visit, thereby elevating the Ziyarat to a celestial act of worship.
